findings.summary: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the return value of `setInterval(...)` is never assigned to it. So in `ws.onclose=function(){clearInterval(pingTimer);setTimeout(connect,3000);}` (line 876), `pingTimer` is always `undefined`, making `clearInterval(pingTimer)` a no-op. Each reconnect re-invokes `connect()`, which starts a fresh `setInterval` that is never cleared -- ping loops from prior connections keep running concurrently after every reconnect. This is precisely the failure mode the brief calls out to prevent (client-driven ping timer from a previous connection must be torn down on close so reconnecting doesn't leave multiple ping loops running concurrently). Fix: `pingTimer=setInterval(function(){...},15000);`.

findings.summary: The new test only greps the served HTML for the literal substrings `setInterval(function(){`, `ws.send('ping')`, and `clearInterval(pingTimer)`. It never executes the script or checks that the interval handle returned by setInterval is actually captured, so it passes unchanged with the assignment bug above (the string `clearInterval(pingTimer)` is present in the source regardless of whether `pingTimer` was ever set). The test gives false confidence that the reconnect-leak requirement was met.
